Visit the County Clerk at 150 N. Seguin, Suite 1037, New Braunfels, TX 78130, or phone 830-221-1230. The clerk's page groups deeds under a Recording (OPR) heading that also covers land records, liens and judgments, military discharges, assumed names, a map and plat viewer and a general research request form.

The same page links an online land records search and a plat viewer with download. The clerk is clerk of the County and Commissioners Courts and recorder of the county under the Texas Constitution, which is why one office holds both your deed and the county's court files.

Public hours at the main office are weekdays, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Staff work until 5:00 p.m., but no walk-ins are taken after 4:30, and a lunch closure runs from noon to 1:00 p.m. Two branch offices serve owners who live away from downtown New Braunfels.

  • Sattler office: 160 Oak Drive, Sattler, TX 78133, phone 830-387-7704
  • Bulverde office: 30470 Cougar Bend, Bulverde, TX 78163, phone 830-387-7620
  • County Court at Law clerks: 199 Main Plaza, 1st Floor, New Braunfels, phone 830-221-1240

Attorneys have had to e-file civil and probate cases with the County Court at Law since January 1, 2015. A paper packet will not work for those departments.

Deliver a signed and acknowledged deed to the clerk's Recording department. The Quick Tips PDF on the clerk's page lists current filing steps, and the fee schedule there was revised July 22, 2025, so look at it before you bring payment.

Texas sets the floor. State law sets a base of $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each added page (Local Government Code 118.012 and 118.013), and records management, archive and technology fees stack on that. The deed must also carry a proper acknowledgment before an authorized officer, or two subscribing witnesses (Property Code 12.001(b)).

The clerk's page also links a property fraud alert page, a good stop for any owner who wants to watch for filings against a house.

sections.h2: What to ask before you file
sections.html:
Ask what the filer must show at the counter, how the instrument will be indexed, and whether the clerk wants the pages in a certain order. Under Senate Bill 16, a 2025 state law that took effect September 1, 2025, a county clerk must ask for photo identification from anyone presenting a document for the real property records, copy the ID, and reject the filing if the person refuses. The law targets deed fraud.

  • Carry a government photo ID for whoever hands over the deed.
  • Confirm the grantee mailing address is printed on the deed.
  • Ask whether the clerk wants payment by check, and who the payee should be.
  • Keep the recording stamp, because title companies ask for the instrument number.

Call the Recording staff at 830-221-1230 to confirm current requirements before you travel.

Sales are held on the Northeast courthouse steps of the historic Comal County Courthouse, 100 Main Plaza, New Braunfels, on the first Tuesday of each month. Commissioners Court ordered sales to follow Property Code Section 51.002, and the county's foreclosure sales page tells inquirers to contact the trustee named on each notice.

A notice on file does not mean the sale will happen on the next date. The trustee decides that, so a seller with a notice should speak with the trustee and a title company before listing.

The Comal Appraisal District, at 900 S. Seguin Ave., New Braunfels, TX 78130, values property and runs exemptions. Its official site is comalad.org, phone 830-625-8597, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Be careful with comalcad.org. That is a private search site paid for by sponsorships and not run by any government agency, so use the district's own address when you file anything.

To protest a value, file by May 15 or by the 30th day after the notice reaches you, whichever comes later. Schools exempt $140,000 of a homestead and $60,000 more for owners 65 or older or disabled. If the prior owner never had the exemption, a buyer who closes after January 1 can still claim it for the remainder of that year.

sections.h2: Comal County housing at a glance
sections.html:
The county added about 100,000 residents between 2010 and 2025. Population was 108,472 in 2010, 161,501 in 2020 and 209,166 in the July 2025 estimate, a 29.6% change from April 2020. It has 87,882 housing units and issued 1,726 building permits in 2025. Owners occupy 76.6% of 71,354 households.

For 2020 to 2024, the median owner-occupied home is valued at $427,200 and median gross rent is $1,603. Residents 65 or older make up 20.8%. Owners in that group keep a school tax ceiling that can carry over proportionately to a new Texas homestead, which helps a seller relocating within Texas.

Any of these can delay closing by days or weeks, and most are cheap to fix when found early. A buyer's lender will not fund until recorded liens are released, and a trustee notice can freeze a sale altogether.

Four situations come up most often, and each leaves a trail in the clerk's records:

  • An unreleased lien or judgment, listed under the clerk's Lien/Judgments service
  • A plat question for land that was split or sold in pieces, which the Plat Viewer helps answer
  • A deceased owner, which sends the file to the County Court at Law probate department
  • A trustee sale notice, which the foreclosure sales page and trustee both track

The clerk takes research requests on its General Research Request form. Have a title company run the full search before you commit to a closing date.

sections.h2: Which Comal County office handles which step
sections.html:
Most of a sale runs through four offices, and all four sit in New Braunfels.

Comal County offices that touch a home sale

Value and exemptionsComal Appraisal District900 S. Seguin Ave., New Braunfels
Foreclosure salesCourthouse steps, first Tuesday100 Main Plaza, New Braunfels

Gather instrument numbers, case numbers and the trustee's name in one folder. Give copies to the title company once escrow opens.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Comal County Clerk?
faqs.a: The main office is at 150 N. Seguin, Suite 1037, New Braunfels, TX 78130, phone 830-221-1230. Branch offices are in Sattler (160 Oak Drive) and Bulverde (30470 Cougar Bend).

faqs.q: When are foreclosure sales held in Comal County?
faqs.a: On the first Tuesday of each month, on the Northeast steps of the historic courthouse at 100 Main Plaza in New Braunfels. Contact the trustee named on the notice with questions.

faqs.q: Is comalcad.org the official Comal Appraisal District website?
faqs.a: No. That site is private, funded by sponsorships and not part of any government agency. The district's official site is comalad.org, and its office is at 900 S. Seguin Ave. in New Braunfels.

faqs.q: Can I e-file probate or civil cases with the Comal County Clerk?
faqs.a: Yes, and attorneys must. Since January 1, 2015 the County Court at Law civil and probate departments take no paper filings from attorneys, so they go through eFileTexas.

faqs.q: What is the usual protest deadline for a Comal County appraisal?
faqs.a: Whichever is later: May 15, or 30 days after you receive the appraisal notice. Check the date on your own notice.
